findings.title: RSA private key loaded from plain env var
findings.description: The private signing key is read directly from an environment variable. In non-dev deploys this should be mounted from Kubernetes secrets or a KMS. The current loader tolerates a raw PEM string with newline escaping, which has bitten the team before.

findings.title: Camunda URL is not allow-listed
findings.description: `CAMUNDA_URL` is used as a literal base for outbound requests. If the env var is ever supplied from user-controlled configuration, it becomes an SSRF vector. Add scheme + host validation.

findings.title: `X-Correlation-ID` forwarded without sanitation
findings.description: Incoming correlation IDs are forwarded as-is. If a client sends a header with CR/LF characters, downstream log lines can be split. Strip non-hex characters before forwarding.

findings.title: Outbox payload contains no schema version
findings.description: Events published to RabbitMQ do not carry a schema version. Consumers rely on duck typing; a breaking change to the payload can silently corrupt projections.

findings.title: `GET /specifications` publicly readable
findings.description: List endpoint is unauthenticated to allow internal service-to-service calls. Consider service-to-service mTLS or a cluster-local network policy — unauthenticated reads of catalog taxonomy are not obviously safe in all deployments.

findings.title: Lock/unlock endpoints reuse admin role
findings.description: Saga worker endpoints reuse the ADMIN role. A dedicated SAGA role (or service account) would narrow the blast radius if a UI-side admin token leaked.

findings.title: Pre-flight validation is not transactional with saga start
findings.description: A specification or price could be deleted between pre-flight check and Camunda process start. Not fatal — the saga compensates — but surfaces confusing 'OfferingPublicationFailed' reasons to operators.

findings.title: Elasticsearch URL allow-list is absent
findings.description: Same class of issue as Camunda URL — trust the env var, nothing else. Add scheme/host validation.

findings.title: Offering description rendered with `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`
findings.description: If the backend ever accepts untrusted markdown or HTML in the description field, this becomes a reflected XSS sink. Today descriptions are plain text, but add explicit sanitization (DOMPurify) before the next schema change.

findings.title: JWT stored in `localStorage`
findings.description: Tokens in localStorage are accessible to any script running on the origin. For a demo this is fine; for production, prefer httpOnly cookies + CSRF tokens.

findings.title: No per-client rate limit
findings.description: The gateway does not rate-limit clients. Identity-service is the obvious target of password spray attacks; consider a sliding window limit on `/auth/login`.

findings.title: Exception handler leaks correlation ID to 500 responses
findings.description: For 500 responses from uncaught exceptions, the handler still surfaces the correlation ID in the response body. That's a feature for operators, a minor information-disclosure concern for external APIs. Decide by threat model.

findings.title: Public key cache has no TTL
findings.description: The identity-service public key is fetched once and cached forever. Key rotation requires a service restart. Add a TTL + background refresh.

findings.title: Entity payloads logged at DEBUG
findings.description: Characteristic payloads are logged at DEBUG level. Low risk (characteristics aren't PII), but worth a guideline so future services don't copy the pattern with sensitive data.

findings.title: `aio-pika` pinned to a minor version behind latest
findings.description: No known CVE; routine hygiene. Bump to the latest minor during the next maintenance window.

findings.title: No currency-whitelist check at lock time
findings.description: Currency validation happens at create/update. The lock path does not re-check. If an admin rewrites the enum between create and publish, a locked price could carry a stale currency. Defense-in-depth only.

findings.title: Retire endpoint does not check ownership
findings.description: Any ADMIN can retire any offering. If the product ever introduces per-team ownership, this route needs an additional check.

findings.title: Search query parsing has no length cap
findings.description: A 10MB `q` param can stress Elasticsearch. Cap input length at the FastAPI layer.

findings.title: `ProtectedRoute` renders children before redirect completes
findings.description: On the first render after an expired token, children briefly mount before the effect fires. Replace with a loading skeleton while the effect runs.
